pr_title: Ensure automations do not execute from a trigger if they are disabled
pr_body:
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
When an automation is turned off, it detaches the triggers, but if a trigger has already started, it would still fire.  We need to check again if the automation is disabled when the trigger fires to ensure it does not execute if it has been disabled.

It would be nicer to cancel in flight triggers, but since `async_initialize_triggers` does not provide a way to cancel triggers that are currently in flight, and there is no guarantee that the triggers are cancellation safe or have even considered cancellation in their design, rejecting the trigger when the automation is disabled seems like the safest course.

I need to split this into two separate PRs because there are two different problems being solved here

1. If the trigger starts and than the automation is disabled, we still run the automation because there is no check to see if the automation is disabled when the trigger fires.  - This one is probably ok to backport
 
2. There is a race disabling the script which means it may not get disabled in time. - This one has been a problem for so long that its likely going to change some semantics so best to fix in dev only and let it roll out in 2024.5 I've broken that out into https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/115325
Production re-testing still looks good

issue_context.title: Race condition issue with automations with the same trigger
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Imagine two automations. First automation sends a notification, second automation stops and disables the first automation. (Automation configuration pasted in YAML below.)

Up until Home Assistant Core 2024.3 the second automation turned of the first automation and prevented it of sending the notification.
Since Core 2024.4 the second automation still turns off the first automation, however the notification still gets send.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2024.4.0

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

core-2024.3.3

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

_No response_

### Link to integration documentation on our website

_No response_

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

**Automation 1**

```
trigger:
  - platform: state
    entity_id:
      - binary_sensor.presence
    for:
      hours: 0
      minutes: 0
      seconds: 5
    to: "on"
condition: []
action:
  - service: notify.mobile_app_iphone
    data:
      message: Test
mode: single
```

**Automation 2**
```
trigger:
  - platform: state
    entity_id:
      - binary_sensor.presence
    to: "on"
condition: []
action:
  - service: automation.turn_off
    target:
      entity_id: automation.testautomation
    data:
      stop_actions: true
mode: single
```


### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

_No response_

### Additional information

If a delay of 1 second is added to the second automation before the first automation gets turned off, then the sequence works as expected:

```
trigger:
  - platform: state
    entity_id:
      - binary_sensor.presence
    to: "on"
condition: []
action:
  - delay:
      hours: 0
      minutes: 0
      seconds: 1
      milliseconds: 0
  - service: automation.turn_off
    target:
      entity_id: automation.testautomation
    data:
      stop_actions: true
mode: single
```
comments:
I presume that `automation.testautomation` refers `automation 1`. With the 5 seconds delay in `automation 1`, there should indeed not be a race condition.  
But I wonder you have another automation to Re-enable `automation 1`. Can that be your race condition?
Besides that this construction is a little wierd. Normally you add a condition in `automation 1` to optionally notify without a need to disable it by the additional `automation 2`

Yes, `automation.testautomation` refers to `automation 1`. And no, there is no other automation to re-enable `automation 1`: I have a) no such automation and b) have live-checked the status of `automation 1` during the above test: it stays off while it gets executed.

I agree that above construction is a little wierd and it is in fact a little more complicated in my setup. However above construction highlights the issue already and that's why I simplified it to be able to better explain it. If real-life example is necessary I can show it.

Furthermore: I am able to workaround this issue with a condition, true, but I would still like to raise awareness that there might be an issue somewhere.
I share your curiosity. As you indicated that the is no 3rd automation, this should work.  I will try to reproduce 🤔

Something has definitely changed with 2024.4.0 release, even though I'm yet to consistently reproduce the regression.

How I observe the regression in my home server:

I have a pair of sensors created using helpers, and one of them is template.
Let's say `sensor.some_entity` and `binary_sensor.some_entity`, and binary sensor uses value of `sensor.some_entity` for its state calculation.

If I use a value of `sensor.some_entity` in automation's condition, but a value of `binary_sensor.some_entity` in some of actions, 

* before 2024.4.0: second entity always has an updated value
* after 2024.4.0: second entity has previous value

It feels like that automations are being triggered before all entity states update which broke quite a few of my automations

It looks like async_disable is intended to detach the triggers but it doesn't seem to always work
even more detail.  This never happens right after HA starts.  It only happens if the automation has been disable and re-enabled

The first time its disabled the triggers are never detached for some reason

2024-04-09 11:45:36.919 WARNING (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.automation.test_race_automation1] Not detaching triggers

So its detaching the trigger fine, but the trigger starts in time so it fires after the automation is already disabled.  

I'm not sure how to fix this one without breaking manually triggering

So there are really two problems here

1. If the trigger starts and than the automation is disabled, we still run the automation because there is no check to see if the automation is disabled when the trigger fires.  - This one is probably ok to backport and should solve this issue. #115305
 
2. There is a race disabling the script which means it may not get disabled in time. - This one has been a problem for so long that its likely going to change some semantics so best to fix in dev only and let it roll out in 2024.5 via #115325

https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/115325 got a bit to complex to fully fix right now so I did a paired down version in https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/115340. Its likely https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/115340 addresses nearly all the cases and I can't actually find one that it does not, but it doesn't have the strong guarantee that  #115325 would have had. Unfortunately that change is too risky right now to make
